title: dpa-review input: a structured description of one Data Processing Agreement
description: Generated from src/dpa_review/contract.py by `make docs`; docs/input-format.md explains every key. The CLI enforces this schema and, beyond it, a few cross-field rules: every key of transfers.mechanisms and of the other per-country objects under transfers is a listed destination, sub-processor names are unique ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, review_date is a calendar date, and every evidence key names a fact the input records. Input that breaks any of them exits 3.

$schema.description: The URL or path of schema/dpa.schema.json, so an editor can check and complete the file as you type. No rule reads it.

agreement.description: Name of the agreement, used as the packet title. No rule reads it.

controller.description: Name of the controller. Labels the transfer evidence graph; no rule reads it.

processor.description: Name of the processor. Labels the transfer evidence graph; no rule reads it.

roles_defined.description: Whether the DPA defines the controller and processor roles. Recorded only: no rule reads it.

review_date.description: The date the transfers are assessed on, as YYYY-MM-DD. The transfer rules read each adequacy decision as it applied on that date: before the date it applies from or after its last day of validity it does not cover the transfer, and before an amendment that changed its scope or validity the transfer goes to review, because the tool models only the decision as last amended. Null or omitted reads the decisions as the adequacy table states them (checks.TABLE_AS_OF). A date after that table date gets a note that later Commission acts are not reflected. A date before 25 May 2018, when the GDPR began to apply (Art. 99(2) GDPR), gets a note on every transfer finding that Directive 95/46/EC governed the transfer and is not modelled; the state does not change.

processing.description: The processing details GDPR Art. 28(3) requires the DPA to set out. Read by the processing.* rules.

subject_matter.description: The subject matter of the processing is stated: true, or a short description. Rule processing.subject_matter.

duration.description: The duration of the processing is stated: true, or a short description. Rule processing.duration.

nature_and_purpose.description: The nature and purpose of the processing are stated: true, or a short description. Rule processing.nature_and_purpose.

data_types.description: The types of personal data processed. Rule processing.data_types: an empty or omitted list is MISSING.

data_subjects.description: The categories of data subjects. Rule processing.data_subjects: an empty or omitted list is MISSING.

includes_non_hr_data.description: Whether non-HR personal data is transferred; null or omitted when the DPA does not say. Read for a dpf transfer: the importer's certification must cover the data transferred.

includes_hr_data.description: Whether HR data from the employment context is transferred; null or omitted when the DPA does not say. Read for a dpf transfer: the importer's certification must cover the data transferred.

art28_clauses.description: The processor clauses GDPR Art. 28(2)-(4) require. Each flag is true when the DPA contains the clause; false, null or omitted when it was not found.

process_on_documented_instructions.description: Art. 28(3)(a): the processor processes only on documented instructions. Rule art28.process_on_documented_instructions.

confidentiality_commitment.description: Art. 28(3)(b): persons authorised to process are bound to confidentiality. Rule art28.confidentiality_commitment.

security_measures_art32.description: Art. 28(3)(c): the processor takes the security measures of Art. 32. Rule art28.security_measures_art32.

subprocessor_authorization.description: Art. 28(2): "specific" (prior specific written authorisation), "general" (general written authorisation) or "none". Rule subprocessor.authorization: "none", null or omitted is MISSING.

subprocessor_flowdown.description: Art. 28(4): the same data-protection obligations are imposed on every sub-processor. Rule subprocessor.flowdown.

assist_data_subject_requests.description: Art. 28(3)(e): the processor assists with data-subject requests. Rule art28.assist_data_subject_requests.

assist_security_breach.description: Art. 28(3)(f): the processor assists with security, breach and DPIA obligations (Art. 32-36). Rule art28.assist_security_breach.

delete_or_return_on_termination.description: Art. 28(3)(g): the processor deletes or returns the data at the end of the services. Rule art28.delete_or_return_on_termination.

audit_and_inspection_rights.description: Art. 28(3)(h): the processor allows and contributes to audits and inspections. Rule art28.audit_and_inspection_rights.

breach_notification.description: Breach-notification terms (GDPR Art. 33(2)). Read by rule breach.processor_notifies.

processor_notifies_controller.description: The processor notifies the controller of a personal-data breach. Rule breach.processor_notifies.

timing.description: The notice period as the DPA words it, e.g. "without undue delay". The rule passes only wording that contains "undue delay" or "without delay"; other wording goes to review.

controller_notifies_authority_art33.description: The controller's own notice to the supervisory authority is addressed. Recorded only: no rule reads it.

subprocessors.description: Every sub-processor the DPA names or authorises. Each one outside the EEA is checked as a transfer (rule transfer.subprocessor.<name>). Record [] when there are none.

name.description: The sub-processor's name. Names must contain a letter or digit and must differ, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation, because rule ids are derived from them.

country.description: Upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the country where it processes the data, e.g. "US" (the United Kingdom is "GB", Greece is "GR").

purpose.description: What the sub-processor does. Labels the graph; no rule reads it.

transfer_mechanism.description: The Chapter V basis for a sub-processor outside the EEA. Null or omitted reads as none. "adequacy": an Art. 45 adequacy decision; "dpf": the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795); "sccs": Art. 46(2)(c); "bcr": Art. 46(2)(b) and 47; "public_bodies_instrument": Art. 46(2)(a); "sa_standard_clauses": Art. 46(2)(d); "code_of_conduct": Art. 46(2)(e) and 40(3); "certification": Art. 46(2)(f) and 42(2); "authorised_clauses": Art. 46(3)(a); "administrative_arrangement": Art. 46(3)(b); "derogation_art49": an Art. 49 derogation.

dpf_certified.description: For a dpf mechanism: the sub-processor is actively certified on the Data Privacy Framework List.

dpf_covers_non_hr_data.description: For a dpf mechanism: the sub-processor's DPF certification covers non-HR data.

dpf_covers_hr_data.description: For a dpf mechanism: the sub-processor's DPF certification covers HR data.

occasional_and_not_repetitive.description: For a derogation_art49 mechanism: the transfer is occasional and not repetitive. Otherwise the derogation is treated like a missing basis.

recipient_type.description: The sub-processor as an importer. What kind of organisation the importer is: "private_commercial" (a private organisation acting in the course of commercial activities), "public_body" (a public authority or body) or "non_profit". Read for Canada (Decision 2002/2/EC, Art. 1 and recital 5: a private commercial organisation is covered, a public body is not, a non-profit goes to review) and Japan (Implementing Decision (EU) 2019/419, Art. 1(1) and recitals 32 and 33: a public body is not covered). Null or omitted leaves the condition unresolved.

scope_carve_out.description: The sub-processor as an importer. "none" when the importer falls within none of the exclusions of Art. 1(2) of the Japanese (Implementing Decision (EU) 2019/419) or Korean (Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/254) decision for the data transferred, "applies" when it falls within one. Null or omitted leaves the condition unresolved.

automated_processing.description: The transfer to the sub-processor. Israel (Decision 2011/61/EU, Art. 1(1)): true when the transfer is automated or the data are subject to further automated processing in Israel, false when neither. Null or omitted leaves the condition unresolved.

transfers.description: Transfers of personal data that the processor makes directly to other countries.

destinations.description: Upper-case ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of every country the processor transfers personal data to directly, and "EPO" for the European Patent Organisation, an international organisation; each is checked (rule transfer.<country>). Record [] when there are none.

mechanisms.description: The Chapter V basis per destination, keyed by a country that destinations lists. A destination without an entry reads as none. "adequacy": an Art. 45 adequacy decision; "dpf": the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795); "sccs": Art. 46(2)(c); "bcr": Art. 46(2)(b) and 47; "public_bodies_instrument": Art. 46(2)(a); "sa_standard_clauses": Art. 46(2)(d); "code_of_conduct": Art. 46(2)(e) and 40(3); "certification": Art. 46(2)(f) and 42(2); "authorised_clauses": Art. 46(3)(a); "administrative_arrangement": Art. 46(3)(b); "derogation_art49": an Art. 49 derogation.

additionalProperties.description: The Chapter V basis for this destination.

dpf_certified.description: For a dpf mechanism, per destination: the importer is actively certified on the Data Privacy Framework List.

additionalProperties.description: The importer is actively certified on the Data Privacy Framework List.

dpf_covers_non_hr_data.description: For a dpf mechanism, per destination: the importer's DPF certification covers non-HR data.

additionalProperties.description: The importer's DPF certification covers non-HR data.

dpf_covers_hr_data.description: For a dpf mechanism, per destination: the importer's DPF certification covers HR data.

additionalProperties.description: The importer's DPF certification covers HR data.

occasional_and_not_repetitive.description: For a derogation_art49 mechanism, per destination: the transfer is occasional and not repetitive. Otherwise the derogation is treated like a missing basis.

additionalProperties.description: The transfer is occasional and not repetitive.

What kind of organisation the importer is: "private_commercial" (a private organisation acting in the course of commercial activities), "public_body" (a public authority or body) or "non_profit". Read for Canada (Decision 2002/2/EC, Art. 1 and recital 5: a private commercial organisation is covered, a public body is not, a non-profit goes to review) and Japan (Implementing Decision (EU) 2019/419, Art. 1(1) and recitals 32 and 33: a public body is not covered). Null or omitted leaves the condition unresolved.

additionalProperties.description: What kind of organisation the importer is.

scope_carve_out.description: Per destination, the importer. "none" when the importer falls within none of the exclusions of Art. 1(2) of the Japanese (Implementing Decision (EU) 2019/419) or Korean (Implementing Decision (EU) 2022/254) decision for the data transferred, "applies" when it falls within one. Null or omitted leaves the condition unresolved.

additionalProperties.description: Whether the importer falls within an exclusion of Art. 1(2).

automated_processing.description: Per destination. Israel (Decision 2011/61/EU, Art. 1(1)): true when the transfer is automated or the data are subject to further automated processing in Israel, false when neither. Null or omitted leaves the condition unresolved.

additionalProperties.description: The transfer is automated or the data are subject to further automated processing.

transfer_impact_assessment.description: A transfer impact assessment is recorded. Read when an Art. 46 safeguard is recorded for a destination or sub-processor in a third country: with no adequacy decision, by rule transfer.impact_assessment; with an adequacy decision that may not cover the importer (the United States and its DPF decision included), by the transfer rule, which asks whether the importer is within the decision's scope.

ccpa.description: California CCPA/CPRA terms, a secondary lens. Omitted reads as not recorded, which goes to review.

service_provider_terms.description: Service-provider terms restricting the sale and retention of personal information are present. Rule ccpa.service_provider_terms.

evidence.description: Where each recorded fact comes from in the DPA, keyed by the fact's path, e.g. {"art28_clauses.subprocessor_flowdown": {"clause": "§ 7.2", "quote": "..."}}. The packet prints it next to the findings that read the fact. A key must name a fact this input records.

additionalProperties.description: The clause and quote that support one recorded fact.

clause.description: Where the fact is in the DPA, e.g. "§ 7.2" or "Annex 3".

quote.description: The DPA's own words, quoted verbatim.
